steps.text: Your first day starts with the People team, who send the contract, the payroll forms and a schedule for the week.
Before you arrive the IT desk prepares your laptop and creates your account in Okta, the single sign-on system that opens every other tool.
You activate Okta on the first morning with someone from the IT desk beside you, and from then on you sign in to mail, chat and the code host through it.
Your buddy has lunch with you in the first week, answers the questions that feel too small to ask anyone else, and checks in once a week for your first two months.

relations.description: claims are submitted in Expensify within a month of paying
approves or rejects the claim, usually within a couple of days
reviews approved claims within 5 days

steps.text: Submit each expense in Expensify within a month of paying, with a photo of the receipt and a one-line reason.
Your manager approves or rejects the claim, usually within a couple of days.
Approved claims then go to Finance, who review them within 5 days and add the amount to your next salary payment.
Finance may ask you for a missing receipt, which pauses the clock until you reply.

entities.name: Incident process
entities.description: How Northwind responds when a customer-facing system breaks.

entities.name: On-call engineer
entities.description: Is paged when a system breaks and leads the response until it is resolved or handed over.

entities.name: PagerDuty
entities.description: Pages the on-call engineer.

entities.name: Incident channel
entities.description: Where everyone working an incident talks, so the timeline stays in one place.

entities.name: Post-mortem
entities.description: A blameless write-up of an incident, due within 3 days of resolution.

relations.description: pages the on-call engineer when a customer-facing system breaks
opens a thread and posts what they know
whoever led the response writes it within 3 days

steps.text: When a customer-facing system breaks, the on-call engineer is paged through PagerDuty.
The on-call engineer acknowledges the page, opens a thread in the incident channel and posts what they know.
The on-call engineer leads until the incident is resolved or hands the lead over to someone else, and says so in the channel.
Within 3 days of resolution, whoever led the response writes a post-mortem.

entities.name: Release process
entities.description: How a release goes from branch to production.

entities.name: Release captain
entities.description: An engineer chosen in turn who runs a release from branch cut to production.

entities.name: Staging
entities.description: Where the release branch is deployed and checked before production.

entities.name: Changelog
entities.description: Lists every change in a release with a link to its pull request.

relations.description: decides when the branch is cut and promotes the build to production
deploys the release branch to staging and runs the checks
writes the changelog once staging looks healthy

steps.text: The captain decides when the release branch is cut, deploys it to staging, and runs the checks there.
When staging looks healthy, the captain writes the changelog, listing every change that ships with a link to its pull request.
The captain then promotes the build to production.
If anything goes wrong after the release, the captain rolls back first and asks questions afterwards.
